Cautiously supportive, but SLOOS tilts the balance more negative. While the FOMC maintains near‑zero rates, continued Treasury and agency MBS purchases, and strong forward guidance, the latest Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (covering 2020:Q3) indicates credit supply remains a headwind:
- Banks reported further tightening of lending standards and terms for C&I loans to firms of all sizes and for commercial real estate loans, citing an uncertain economic outlook and reduced risk tolerance.
- Household credit also saw tighter standards (e.g., credit cards and autos); residential mortgage demand was strong on low rates but standards were generally tighter across segments.
- C&I loan demand remained weak, and banks anticipated deterioration in credit quality in affected segments.

These SLOOS findings imply bank intermediation is restraining the transmission of accommodative policy to the real economy, reinforcing downside risks flagged in the FSR (e.g., SME strain, CRE stress). Net tone: slightly more negative than previously assessed.
